input.recommendation: Remove the hardcoded secret and use GitHub Secrets with ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}.
input.description: Hardcoded secret in workflow environment block.
Use of pull_request_target with checkout of untrusted PR head.
input.recommendation: Do not check out untrusted PR head code when using pull_request_target.
input.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/auto-label.yml uses pull_request_target and checks out the PR head ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}.

input.recommendation: Always sanitize or use environment variables to pass PR event data into shell scripts.
input.description: Untrusted PR event input used in a shell script without sanitization.
input.evidence: The greeting workflow uses ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} directly in a shell command. An attacker could inject commands into the PR title.
package.json exists but no package-lock.json or similar lockfile is present in the repository.
input.recommendation: Generate and commit a package-lock.json file.
Add an explicit permissions block to restrict the GITHUB_TOKEN to the minimum necessary scopes.
input.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/auto-label.yml uses pull_request_target but does not define a permissions block, granting default (often excessive) permissions.
input.description: Missing permissions block in security-sensitive workflow.

input.summary: The audit identified several security, collaboration, and dependency management issues in the repository. These include a hardcoded secret in a workflow, dangerous use of `pull_request_target` with checkout of untrusted PR content, potential command injection in PR greetings, missing dependency lockfiles, and missing explicit workflow permissions in sensitive workflows. The repository is intentionally vulnerable for testing purposes.
